originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 source assumes global uniform \(C_0\) and explicitly leaves removal of that hypothesis open. The inspected 2025 noncompact theorem uses topological expansivity and a different entropy-like invariant \(e^*\), so it does not imply the present geometrically-separating, ordinary-upper-capacity statement. Focused repository and web searches found no statement localizing the small-time hypothesis to the periodic-point set. A specifically named but bibliographically incomplete 2026 preprint remains a disclosed residual risk.

value.rationale: The primary source explicitly identifies the global uniform \(C_0\) assumption as the unresolved obstruction in its noncompact Bowen–Walters theorem. Localizing the needed regularity to periodic points materially narrows that open problem: any counterexample beyond the new theorem must fail uniform small-time control already along periodic orbits. The strict entropy-preserving example shows this is a genuine enlargement of the theorem, not a cosmetic reformulation, while retaining the same standard entropy and periodic-orbit data.
